title: Annotatio V §.IV THIRD genus (2)–(3): sensual; Capernaite; flesh profits nothing — stop mid-§.IV
pass_a_gloss: (2) It would be Sensual, or exposed to taste, because every food orally eaten is felt to be eaten; but no one has thus far felt Christ’s Body eaten by himself — not even the believer mystically united to Christ, however often and with how great faith and persuasion of obtaining closer Communion with Christ he has approached the Sacred Supper. Nay it would be Capernaite by the very fact that it is Oral, seeing that thus it is Corporal and Carnal and so Capernaite — whether immediately or by means of bread; whether finished in a physical or hyperphysical mode; whether momentary and ending in the mouth, or with delay of time the eaten is carried to the throat and at last to the stomach. (3) Considered alone and by itself (a) it avails nothing, John 6:63 — ‘but the flesh profits nothing,’ says Christ; Yet He wills not that His flesh viewed by itself avails nothing, but either flesh in opposition to the Spirit, or, if Christ’s flesh is regarded, Christ’s flesh eaten as Capernaitically and Oraliter as only Sacramentally is understood: for so Theophylact on this place: ‘but the flesh — that is, to receive them fleshly — profits nothing,’ And our Zwingli on the same: CHRIST’s Flesh profits very much indeed, nay immensely — but slain, not carnally chewed. Slain it saves us from slaughter, not carnally eaten. (b) It does not vivify, whether it be of bread or of Christ’s flesh, with or without bread: Oral Eating of bread cannot vivify — for this is the work of God alone; Nor does the proper Eating of Christ’s flesh vivify; for when the Capernaites understood this, Christ answers: It is the Spirit that vivifies; the Flesh profits nothing.
pass_b_english: THIRD (2)–(3): Oral would be sensual (felt by taste) — yet no one, not even the mystic believer, has ever felt Christ’s Body eaten. By being Oral it is Capernaite — whether immediate or through bread, physical or hyperphysical, mouth-only or down to the stomach.

Alone it avails nothing (Jn 6:63): Theophylact and Zwingli read ‘flesh profits nothing’ of Capernaite/oral (or merely sacramental) chewing — slain flesh saves; carnal chewing does not vivify. Stop mid-§.IV (exception / further genera remain).
source_text: (2) Sensualis foret, seu gustui exposita, quia omnis cibus, oraliter manducatus, sentitur manducari; sed Corpus Christi nemo hactenus sensit à se manducari, ne fidelis quidem Christóque mysticè unitus, quotiescunque etiam, quantâque fide & persuasione, arctiorem cum Christo Communionem consequendi, Cœnam S. accessit. Quin Capernaitica foret, eô ipsô, quia Oralis, quandoquidem sic Corporalis & Carnalis eóque Capernaitica, sive immediatè, sive mediante pane, fiat; sive physicô, sive hyperphysicô modô perficiatur; sive momentanea sit inque ore desinat, sive cum mora temporis ad guttur tandemque ad stomachum, manducatum deferatur. (3) Sola & per se considerata (a) non valet quicquam, Johan. 6, 63. he de sarx ouk ophelei ouden dicit Christus; Vult verò, non carnem suam per se spectatam, nihil quicquam valere, sed, vel carnem in oppositione Spiritûs, vel, si caro Christi respicitur, intelligitur caro Christi tam Capernaiticè & Oraliter, quàm tantùm Sacramentaliter comesta: sic enim Theophylactus in hunc locum: he de sarx tout’ esti to sarkikôs auta endechesthai, ouden ophelei, Et Zwinglius noster in eundem: Caro CHRISTI plurimùm omnino, imò immensum prodest, sed casa, non carnaliter ambesa. Casa nos servat à cæde, non, carnaliter manducata. (b) Non vivificat, sive sit panis, sive carnis Christi, cum, vel sine pane: Oralis Manducatio panis, non potest vivificare: hoc enim est opus solius Dei; Nec carnis Christi Manducatio propria vivificat; hanc enim cùm Capernaitæ intelligerent, respondet Christus. Spiritus est qui vivificat, Caro non prodest quicquam.
notes: THIRD (2)–(3): sensual; Capernaite; Jn 6:63; mid-§.IV stop.
